name: The Conduit
body:
The conduit has an inborn connection to a force of nature so vast that they are only touching the vast edge of a cosmic bubble. They siphon this power and channel it through themselves.

Hybrid Class: The conduit is a hybrid of the druid and sorcerer classes.

Role: The conduit can range from support caster, to healer, debilitator or destroyer. In all cases they are better served in the back line away from direct danger unless in a polymorphed form, though even some their lower base attack limits their effectiveness in this regard.

Alignment: Any. Conduits can be any alignment, but many, especially those connected to more violent forces of nature, tend to be chaotic.

Hit Die: d8

Starting Wealth: 2d6 × 10 gp (average 70 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills: The conduit’s class skills are Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Fly (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Points Per Level: 4 + Intelligence Modifier

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the conduit.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Conduits are proficient with all simple weapons and light armor and shields.

Spellcasting

A conduit casts arcane spells drawn primarily from the druid spell list and their force of nature. See page 2 for more information on how these spells are split. They can cast any spell they know without preparing it ahead of time. To learn or cast a spell, a conduit must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a conduit’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the conduit’s Charisma modifier. Like other spellcasters, a conduit can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on the spells per day table. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Charisma score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells).

A conduit’s selection of spells is extremely limited. A conduit begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of their choice, half of which may be from the druid spell list, the other half must be from the spells noted by their force of nature. At each new conduit level, they gain one or more new spells, as indicated on the spells known table below, the split between druid spell list spells and spells from their force of nature is shown as the left side of the “+” is druid spell list, the right side is the force of nature list. Unlike spells per day, the number of spells a conduit knows is not affected by their Charisma score; the numbers on spells known table are fixed.

If a given spell is on both lists, it may be used for either for the purposes of splitting their spells known.

Upon reaching 4th level, and at every even-numbered conduit level after that (6th, 8th, and so on), a conduit can choose to learn a new spell in place of one they already know. In effect, the conduit loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged and the spell must still adhere to the split between druid spell list and force of nature spell lists. A conduit may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that they gain new spells known for the level.

Unlike a druid, a conduit need not prepare their spells in advance. They can cast any spell they know at any time, assuming they have not yet used up their spells per day for that spell level.

Cantrips: Conduits learn a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, as noted on the spells known table below.

These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume any slots and may be used again. These spells may be from the druid spell list or from the spells provided by the conduit’s force of nature, they need not be split between the two lists.

Connection Ability: At 1st level, a conduit gains some amazing powers by channeling their connection to their force of nature. The conduit gains an additional connection ability at 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter.

Connection Spell: At 1st level, the conduit gains an additional spell known provided by their force of nature. This initial spell is a cantrip. At 2nd level and every even level thereafter, except for 20th level, the conduit gains another bonus spell known of increasingly higher spell levels as shown in the conduit’s force of nature.

Eschew Materials: A conduit gains Eschew Materials as a bonus feat at 1st level.

Force of Nature (Su)

The conduit forms a connection with the raw power of the forces that make up reality. At 1st level, they express their connection to a specific force of nature. Once the force of nature is chosen it cannot be changed. In addition to the connection powers and spells provided, it provides a unique primal empathy, natural skill, and natural movement. Additionally, the force of nature provides a means of communing with the force of nature to regain abilities after an 8-hour rest and a manifestation of the connection.

For more information, see forces of nature.

Primal Ability: The conduit has abilities that draw upon the primal forces of nature. At 1st level, then 3rd level and every 4 levels thereafter, the conduit gains a primal ability, see the primal abilities section on page XX2 for more information. Unless the ability says otherwise, a primal ability may only be taken once.

Additionally, the conduit’s force of nature may modify or improve the primal ability as listed in the ability’s description.

Primal Empathy (Su)

The conduit’s connection to their force of nature gives them an innate ability to communicate with creatures that share a similar connection. See the force of nature description for which creatures qualify and how the communication manifests. In all cases this acts as the spell speak with animals and/or tongues.

Primal Pool (Su)

The conduit is filled with the power of nature which allows them to perform feats beyond the capabilities of their peers. When the conduit communes with their force of nature to regain their spells, they gain a number of primal points equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Their primal points go up and down throughout the day but usually cannot go higher than their Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). The conduit spends primal points to activate some of their force of nature abilities, and may regain primal points in the following way:

Spell Power: The conduit may draw upon the energies they have stored for casting their spells as a swift action to restore primal energies. For every 5 levels of spells expended, the conduit may regain 1 primal point. The 5 levels may be any combination of spells so long as the total spell-slot-levels equal 5 or more.

In addition to the abilities granted by their force of nature the conduit may also expend a primal point to increase the caster level of a spell being cast by 1. Doing so is not an action but the point must be expended as the spell is being cast and before the effects are applied.

Natural Skill (Ex)

At 2nd level, the conduit has a knack for a skill related to their force of nature.

The conduit gains a bonus on checks with that skill equal to 1/2 their class level. At 8th level, the conduit may take 10 with the skill even when in a situation that would normally not allow them to. At 16th level, they may take 20 with the skill without taking extra time.

Additionally, the skill becomes a class skill if it is not already.

Natural Movement (Su)

At 6th level, the conduit is in tune with their force of nature and may move in circumstances that would inhibit others. Their movement is not inhibited by natural difficult terrain like loose rubble, foliage, sand or snow. Difficult terrain created by a spell still inhibits the conduit, however, their force of nature allows them to ignore other difficult terrain circumstances.

Natural Revitalization (Su)

Beginning with 10th level, if the conduit does not have any primal points remaining, they may commune with their force of nature as outlined its description for 10 minutes and regain 1 primal point. This ability cannot be used if the conduit has primal points in their pool.

Timeless Body (Ex)

The conduit is no longer affected by the ravages of time. At 14th level, the conduit no longer takes ability score penalties for aging and cannot be magically aged. Any penalties they may have already incurred, however, remain in place. Bonuses still accrue, and the conduit still dies of old age when their time is up.

Avatar of Nature (Su)

The conduit becomes a force of nature unto themselves. At 20th level, the conduit may use natural revitalization regardless of the number of primal points in their pool but cannot go above their maximum pool. Additionally, all durations of primal abilities are doubled.

Forces of nature are broad and overwhelming forces that make up reality. The conduit forms a connection with these forces and uses them to empower themselves. The DCs for any abilities gained from a force of nature is 10 + 1/2 the conduit’s class levels + their Charisma modifier.

In addition to the abilities, spells and other abilities provided by their force of nature, it provides an aesthetic manifestation of its power within the conduit and a method with which to commune with the force of nature to regain spells and primal points. While general examples are provided, be creative in how you would like these aspects to be shown.

When looking at the connection spells the level the spell is gained and the spell level of the spell are listed, the class level on the left, spell level on the right.
